title: Breastfeeding factors and gut microbiota dynamics in infants during the first year: a Beijing cohort study.
justification: Cohort of 67 infants is exclusively (50.7%) or predominantly (49.3%, >80% breast milk) breastfed; the only feeding-mode contrast analyzed is exclusive vs. predominant breastfeeding over time -- there is no formula-fed comparator arm.

title: Association of feeding methods in early life with gut microbiota in neonates.
justification: All 265 neonates were recruited from a NICU population (not just the preterm stratum); antibiotic exposure was 78-86% and pediatric clinical disease (e.g., respiratory ~68%) was prevalent across all feeding and gestational-age groups, so the full-term subgroup is still a NICU/clinical cohort rather than a genuinely healthy term subgroup.

title: Maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides influence the infant gut resistome.
justification: Primary exposure contrast is exclusive breastfeeding (n=40) vs. non-exclusive breastfeeding (n=17), where non-exclusive lumps mixed feeding (n=13) and exclusive formula (n=4) into one group; formula is not isolated as a distinct comparator as required.

title: Impact of Infant Feeding Mode on Gut Microbiome Composition in Early Life: Evidence from an Egyptian Cohort.
justification: 48 healthy full-term infants (>=37wk GA, birth weight 2.5-4.0kg, no congenital anomalies/prematurity/GI-metabolic disease), aged 0-6 months, in three distinct feeding groups (exclusive BF n=12, exclusive formula n=18, mixed n=18); 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing with alpha/beta diversity and taxonomic composition reported.

title: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health.
justification: Lifelines NEXT: 714 mother-infant pairs (92.7% full-term, general population birth cohort not NICU-recruited), shotgun metagenomics of infant stool at 7 timepoints (2wk-12mo); reports breastfed vs. formula-fed vs. mixed-fed as distinct groups with alpha diversity and taxonomic composition differences (e.g. formula-fed infants had higher alpha diversity than breastfed, FDR=0.001).

title: Early-life gut microbiome-metabolome development trajectories in Chinese infants: a decentralized real-world evidence study.
justification: The formula-fed arm received an open-label formula supplemented with prebiotics (scGOS/lcFOS 9:1) compared against a breastfed reference group; an unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast cannot be isolated since all formula-fed infants received the prebiotic-supplemented product.

title: Effects of an infant formula containing a whey protein concentrate on feeding tolerance and markers of intestinal immune defense in Chinese infants.
justification: Fortified-formula trial: FF group received an experimental formula enriched with whey protein concentrate (alpha-lactalbumin), MFGM, and sn-2 palmitate specifically designed to mimic human milk composition, vs. a BF reference group; a standard unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast cannot be isolated.

title: Protect the Heart by Protecting the Gut-Human Milk and the Gut Microbiota of Neonates With Critical Congenital Heart Defects.
justification: This is an opinion/commentary column in the journals Breastfeeding/Nutrition section discussing the authors own prior n=4 dissertation study; no new primary data reported, and the discussed cohort is neonates with critical congenital heart defects (a clinical condition defining the population).

title: Infant fecal microbiome dysbiosis varies by feeding type in setting of severe bronchiolitis.
justification: All 27 infants were hospitalized with bronchiolitis (cases=severe, controls=mild bronchiolitis); the cohort is defined entirely by this acute respiratory illness, not a healthy infant population.

title: Integrated Analysis of Gut Microbiota and Metabolome Profiling Reveals the Effects of Feeding Approaches on Infants Gut Microenvironment.
justification: 44 healthy full-term 6-month-old infants, exclusively BF (n=27) vs exclusively FF (n=17), verified by structured interview and 3-day dietary records; excluded congenital defects, antibiotics/probiotics exposure, chronic disease; full-length 16S rRNA sequencing with taxonomic composition reported.

title: Breastfeeding may lessen socioeconomic disparities in child health through differences in the infant gut microbiome.
justification: CHILD cohort (n=1479 with shotgun metagenomic stool data at 3mo/1yr) + COPSAC2010 replication; general population (not clinical/NICU recruited); reports taxonomic composition (alpha/beta diversity, species-level) differences by current breastfeeding status vs. not breastfed, with shotgun metagenomic sequencing.

title: Effects of infant formula supplied with medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols and sn-2 palmitate on fecal lipid metabolome and microbiota profiles in healthy term infants: a parallel-controlled study.
justification: 173 healthy term infants in 3 groups: novel structured-lipid formula (n=64), standard control formula (Contr-F, n=44), and exclusively breastfed (n=65); the standard-formula-vs-breastfed contrast is isolable via the Contr-F arm. 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing at 30d/90d with genus-level composition reported.

title: Effects of feeding type on gut microbiota and atopic dermatitis in cesarean delivered infants: a combined birth cohort study.
justification: 129 cesarean-delivered infants (no significant gestational age differences across groups, term per demographics) in 3 groups: exclusively breastfed (n=12), standard formula (n=94), probiotic-fortified formula (n=23); breastfed-vs-standard-formula contrast is isolable via Groups A/B. 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing at 6-8 weeks with diversity and taxonomic composition reported.

title: Breastfed infants receiving formula supplementation show altered lipid and gut microbiota profiles at 3 months of age.
justification: n=519 infants across two European cohorts classified into exclusive breastfeeding (EBF), mixed feeding (MF), and exclusive formula feeding (EFF) as distinct groups at 3 months; shotgun metagenomics of stool with microbiota diversity/richness and taxonomic composition reported by feeding type.

title: Impact of medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols and sn-2 palmitate on temperament development in term infants: potential role of gut Bifidobacterium.
justification: 179 healthy full-term infants (37-42wk GA, no congenital anomalies/feeding intolerance) in 3 groups: MLCT/sn-2-palmitate formula (IG, n=65), standard control formula (CG, n=48), exclusively breastfed (BG, n=66); CG-vs-BG provides an isolable unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast. 16S rRNA sequencing with Bifidobacterium/Blautia abundance reported by group at 1 and 3 months.

title: Human Milk and Infant Gut Microbiome in Association With Infant Fecal Metabolome and Child Blood Pressure.
justification: CHILD cohort inclusion was infants born at >=35 weeks gestation (includes late-preterm 35-36wk infants) with no separate healthy-term-only (>=37wk) subgroup analysis reported; primary outcome is also child blood pressure rather than gut microbiome composition.

title: Gut microbiota responses to complementary food sources differ by milk feeding type.
justification: Primary exposure under study is solid/complementary food source (homemade vs. commercial vs. mixed) at 6 months and its association with gut microbiota at 1 year; milk feeding type (human milk/formula/combination) is used only as an effect-modifier/stratification variable, not as the directly compared exposure.

title: Early-Life Demographic Factors Shape Gut Microbiome Patterns Associated with Rotavirus Gastroenteritis Severity.
justification: Case-control study of 120 infants with laboratory-confirmed rotavirus gastroenteritis vs. 45 healthy controls; the primary comparison is RVGE cases vs. controls, with feeding mode examined only as a secondary demographic covariate, not as the primary exposure-comparison.

title: Associations of Lactoferrin-Fortified Formula with Infant Growth and Gut Microbiota: A Real-World Observational Study.
justification: 111 term Chinese infants (age 6-12mo) in 3 propensity-matched groups: lactoferrin-fortified formula (LF, n=37), standard control formula (CF, n=37), exclusive breastfeeding (BF, n=37); CF-vs-BF provides an isolable unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast. 16S rRNA sequencing (n=81) with alpha/beta diversity and taxonomic composition reported.

title: Effect of antibiotics in the first week of life on faecal microbiota development.
justification: 182 term-born infants (56 antibiotic-exposed + 126 healthy controls), 16S rRNA sequencing from birth including 3-week/3-month/1-year timepoints; reports a direct breastfed-vs-formula-fed taxonomic composition comparison (breastfed infants had lower Enterobacteriaceae and faster recovery than formula-fed after antibiotic exposure).

title: Milk IgA promotes symbionts and limits pathobionts in the early life gut.
exclusion_reason: Animal, in vitro, ex vivo, or gut-simulator model
justification: Entire study uses Pigr-/- mouse model (SIgA-deficient mice) with oral gavage colonization experiments; no human infant data.

title: Dynamics of gut metabolome and microbiota maturation during early life.
justification: Breastfeeding is analyzed as a binary current-feeding status/duration variable (any current breastfeeding yes/no; exclusive BF duration), not against a formula-fed comparator group, and the authors explicitly state the sample lacks an adequate number of exclusively formula-fed infants.

title: Associations of diet, race, and other environmental factors with antimicrobial resistance genes in the gut bacterial communities of pregnant women and 3-month-old infants.
justification: Resistome/ARG abundance was quantified by SmartChip qPCR normalized to 16S rRNA gene copy number via qPCR, not by sequencing-based taxonomic profiling, and no bacterial taxonomic composition is reported.

title: Influence of Feeding Pattern on Infant Growth: A Longitudinal Study with Gut Microbiome Insights.
justification: The microbiome subset (n=27) was analyzed only longitudinally by sampling timepoint (birth/6wk/14wk/36wk), not stratified by feeding group (EBF/MF/FF); feeding-pattern group comparisons were reported only for growth, infection, and antibiotic-exposure outcomes, not for taxonomic composition.

title: Partially hydrolyzed, whey-based infant formula with six human milk oligosaccharides, B. infantis LMG11588, and B. lactis CNCM I-3446 is safe, well tolerated, and improves gut health: a staged analysis of a randomized trial.
justification: RCT in healthy full-term infants (>=37wk GA) with three isolable groups: unsupplemented control formula (CTRL), HMO/probiotic-supplemented formula (SYN), and a non-randomized exclusively breastfed reference; CTRL-vs-BF bifidobacteria/taxonomic composition comparison reported via shotgun metagenomics at 3 months.

title: Breastfeeding and the milk resistome shape the establishment and transmission of antibiotic resistance genes in the infant gut microbiome.
justification: Although metagenomic sequencing was used, all reported outcomes are resistome/ARG load, composition, and bacterial-ARG co-occurrence networks; no standard whole-community bacterial taxonomic composition (overall relative abundance, alpha/beta diversity) by feeding group is reported, analogous to a resistome-only study with no bacterial taxonomic composition.

title: Breastfeeding and early Bifidobacterium-driven microbial colonization shape the infant gut resistome.
justification: The breastfed-vs-formula comparisons reported (N=40 BF vs N=4 FF at 1 month) are limited to ARG load/resistome composition; standard bacterial taxonomic composition (species/genus relative abundance, Fig 2B/3A) was analyzed by Bifidobacterium-abundance clustering and age, explicitly independent of feeding mode, so no bacterial taxonomic composition difference by feeding group is reported.

title: Bifidobacterium deficit in United States infants drives prevalent gut dysbiosis.
justification: My Baby Biome study, n=412 US infants aged 1-3 months, general-population decentralized cross-sectional cohort; shotgun metagenomics directly compares species-level abundance (e.g., B. infantis, pathogenic species) between exclusively breastfed and non-breastfed (formula+mixed) infants.

title: Milk phospholipid-coated lipid droplets modulate the infant gut microbiota and metabolome influencing weight gain.
justification: Both formula arms (Control and Test) are supplemented with prebiotic scGOS/lcFOS (0.8 g/100 mL), differing only in lipid-droplet structure, so no unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast can be isolated.

title: Influence of feeding habit and duration on infant gut microbiome - a 6 month pilot study.
justification: Full-term INFAMILK cohort subset, n=23 divided into Exclusive Breastfed (n=6), BreastFed_4 (n=6), BreastFed_8 (n=6), and Formula Fed (n=5) groups; shotgun metagenomics shows Exc Breast Fed had lowest alpha diversity and distinct composition vs Formula Fed group.

title: Bifidogenic Effect of 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL) on the Gut Microbiome of Healthy Formula-Fed Infants: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
justification: Both formula arms are prebiotic-supplemented (HMO/2-FL group and a GOS/FOS control group containing 4 g/L GOS+FOS); there is no unsupplemented-formula arm, so an unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast cannot be isolated.

title: Exclusive breastfeeding is associated with the gut microbiome maturation in infants according to delivery mode.
justification: Fewer than 5% of the cohort were never breastfed, so the comparison is exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) vs. non-EBF, with non-EBF comprised mainly of mixed (breast milk + formula) feeding; the authors explicitly state they were unable to directly compare breastfeeding versus formula/never-breastfeeding.

title: Restoration of gut microbiota with a specific synbiotic-containing infant formula in healthy Chinese infants born by cesarean section.
justification: Both formula arms are supplemented: Test = synbiotic (scGOS/lcFOS + B. breve M-16V) and Control = prebiotic-only (scGOS/lcFOS); no unsupplemented standard-formula arm exists to isolate against the breastfed reference group.

title: Priority effects, nutrition and milk glycan-metabolic potential drive Bifidobacterium longum subspecies dynamics in the infant gut microbiome.
justification: AIMS cohort plus four public metagenomic datasets restricted to healthy, full-term, vaginally-delivered infants; LASSO regression on metagenomic sequencing data reports breastfeeding positively and formula-feeding negatively associated with B. longum subsp. longum abundance at 1 month, a differential-abundance composition outcome by feeding mode.

title: Fecal Microbiome and Metabolomic Profiles of Mixed-Fed Infants Are More Similar to Formula-Fed than Breastfed Infants.
justification: STRONG Kids2 cohort, 75 healthy term infants (GA ~39.5wk) with distinct BF (n=25), FF (n=25), MF (n=25) groups at 6 weeks; metagenomic sequencing shows alpha/beta diversity and composition differ between BF and FF/MF groups.

title: Antibiotic exposure is associated with minimal gut microbiome perturbations in healthy term infants.
justification: Prospective cohort of n=323 healthy term infants with shotgun metagenomics; although the primary exposure is antibiotics, breastfeeding status (any breastmilk vs. exclusively formula) is directly compared and shows significant overall taxonomic composition and species-level differences (Bifidobacterium, E. coli, Klebsiella, Akkermansia, Bacteroides/Clostridia) at 4 and 12 months.

title: First-year dynamics of the anaerobic microbiome and archaeome in infants' oral and gastrointestinal systems.
justification: Healthy term infants (n=30, mean GA 39.3wk) with shotgun metagenomics of monthly stool samples through 1 year; GIT (gut) microbiome composition (alpha/beta diversity, taxon abundance) is directly compared between dynamically-defined breastfed (BF) and non-breastfed (NBF) groups, with NBF status tracking formula feeding (56.7% ever formula-fed).

title: Microbiota, metabolic profiles and immune biomarkers in infants receiving formula with added bovine milk fat globule membrane: a randomized, controlled trial.
justification: RCT in term infants (37-42wk GA), 3 isolable groups: Control (standard bovine formula, unsupplemented), INV-MFGM (MFGM-added formula), and HM (human milk reference); 16S rRNA sequencing shows Control vs HM differ in diversity, richness, and composition (Jaccard/Bray-Curtis) at Day 60.

title: Metal availability shapes early life microbial ecology and community succession.
justification: IGraM prospective cohort (healthy infants, up to n=47 integrated), shotgun metagenomic sequencing; formula-fed infants showed higher gut metal levels and distinct microbial community composition (higher Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Klebsiella) compared to breastfed infants.

title: Microbial colonization programs are structured by breastfeeding and guide healthy respiratory development.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study inclusion criterion is >35 weeks gestation, which includes late-preterm (35-36wk) infants, and no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis is reported (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155).

title: Influence of Feeding Practices on Intestinal Microbiota Composition in Healthy Chinese Infants: A Prospective Cohort Study.
justification: 217 healthy infants, GA >=37wk, three groups (exclusively direct breastfeeding, predominantly expressed breast milk, exclusively formula-fed), 16S V3-V4 sequencing at 6 weeks; formula-fed group showed significantly higher species richness/diversity and distinct taxonomic composition (Firmicutes, Bacteroides, Streptococcus, Veillonella) vs breastfed groups.

title: Breast milk components modulate gut microbiota to increase susceptibility to atopic dermatitis in early life.
justification: This is a commentary discussing and interpreting a separate primary study (Jiang et al., published in Gut) on breast milk arachidonic acid and AD; it presents no new primary human data of its own.

title: Unravelling the evolutionary dynamics of antibiotic resistance genes in the infant gut microbiota during the first four months of life.
justification: The breastfeeding-vs-formula comparisons reported are limited to ARG/resistome composition (PCA by lactation mode, GLMM on ARG load); the 16S-based microbiota composition (alpha/beta diversity, taxa) was analyzed only by age/timepoint and used as covariates predicting ARG load, not reported as a direct taxonomic composition comparison between breastfed and formula-fed infants.

title: Longitudinal changes in bifidobacterial population during the first two years of life.
justification: INCA cohort, 196 term infants (median GA 39.9wk [39.0-40.9]) selected as exclusively breastfed or exclusively formula-fed; 16S-23S ITS sequencing shows feeding mode significantly affects bifidobacterial species-level composition, with effects lasting until 6 months.

title: Diurnal rhythmicity of infant fecal microbiota and metabolites: A randomized controlled interventional trial with infant formula.
justification: RCT with 210 infants and four formula arms plus exclusively breastfed reference; formula A is an unsupplemented placebo isolable from breastfed group, with 16S/shallow metagenomic sequencing showing taxonomic composition and bifidobacterial abundance differences by feeding group.

title: Complement(ing) the microbiome in infants through breastmilk.
justification: This is a Research Highlight commentary summarizing a separate mouse study (Wan et al., Cell) on maternal complement and breastmilk; it presents no new primary data and the underlying study is a mouse model, not human infants.

title: Complement in maternal milk shapes the infant microbiome.
justification: This is a Nature Reviews Immunology In brief commentary summarizing a separate mouse study (Xu et al., Cell 2024) on complement in breast milk; it presents no new primary data and the underlying study is a mouse model.

title: Divergent maturational patterns of the infant bacterial and fungal gut microbiome in the first year of life are associated with inter-kingdom community dynamics and infant nutrition.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study inclusion criterion is delivery after 35 weeks gestation, which includes late-preterm (35-36wk) infants, and no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis is reported (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155 and #488).

title: Metagenomic Characterisation of the Gut Microbiome and Effect of Complementary Feeding on Bifidobacterium spp. in Australian Infants.
justification: ORIGINS Project cohort, 6-month-old Australian infants, preterm and antibiotic-exposed excluded; shotgun metagenomic sequencing shows predominantly formula-fed infants had higher microbiome diversity than predominantly breastfed infants, with distinct taxonomic composition differences.

title: Influence of feeding practices in the composition and functionality of infant gut microbiota and its relationship with health.
justification: 55 mother-infant pairs classified as BF (n=20), FF (n=16, no probiotic strain), CF (n=19); eligibility was GA 36-42wk but achieved mean GA was 38.1+-1.8wk (predominantly term); 16S V3-V4 sequencing showed BF group had highest microbiota diversity vs FF.

title: Precocious infant fecal microbiome promotes enterocyte barrier dysfuction, altered neuroendocrine signaling and associates with increased childhood obesity risk.
justification: The primary studied exposure/outcome is gut microbiota class (GMC1-3, derived by unsupervised DMM clustering) versus childhood obesity risk; breastfeeding status is used only as a covariate/confounder and background characteristic of the GMC groups, with no direct statistical comparison of taxonomic composition between breastfed and formula-fed groups reported.

title: Assessing the impact of pregnancy and birth factors on the maternal and infant microbiota.
justification: For infant stool samples, only delivery mode and infant sex were examined as covariates of microbiota composition; breastfeeding was tested as a covariate only for infant salivary (oral) microbiota, so no breastfed-vs-formula-fed comparison of gut/stool composition is reported.

title: Human leukocyte antigen-dependent colonization of Lactobacillus in the early-life gut.
justification: The ABIS cohort stool samples span 0.3 to 37.2 months of age (mean 11.94 months), and the primary statistical association between active breastfeeding and Lactobacillus abundance/presence is computed across this full mixed-age pooled sample rather than a separately extractable 0-12-month subset.

title: Maternal breastfeeding is associated with offspring microbiome diversity; a secondary analysis of the MicrobeMom randomized control trial.
justification: MicrobeMom cohort, n=118 healthy mother-infant pairs (median GA ~40.2wk), shotgun metagenomic sequencing at 1 month; adjusted regression shows exclusive/any breastfeeding (vs. not breastfeeding, ~31-35% of cohort) directly associated with infant alpha diversity (Shannon, observed species) and beta diversity (PC2).

title: The correlation of the intestinal with pharyngeal microbiota in early neonates.
justification: 20 healthy full-term neonates sampled days 0 and 5-7, 16S rRNA sequencing of stool and oropharyngeal samples; compares exclusive breastfeeding vs limited formula feeding (40-60%) groups directly on intestinal microbiota composition.

title: Breastfeeding and the major fermentation metabolite lactate determine occurrence of Peptostreptococcaceae in infant feces.
justification: Swiss CARE birth cohort, 69 mother-infant pairs grouped as exclusively-BF (n=38), partially-BF (n=17), and non-BF/exclusively formula-fed (n=14); quantitative microbiota profiling (16S rRNA sequencing + qPCR) shows significant alpha/beta diversity and family-level composition differences by feeding group at 3, 6, and 12 months.

title: Infant Formula Supplemented with Five Human Milk Oligosaccharides Shifts the Fecal Microbiome of Formula-Fed Infants Closer to That of Breastfed Infants.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants (37-42wk GA, <=14 days at enrollment), three groups: breastmilk (BM), 5HMO-mix formula, and unsupplemented IF control; shotgun metagenomic sequencing shows IF control vs BM differ significantly in bifidobacteria abundance and composition from Week 1 onward.

title: The Gut Microbiota Differ in Exclusively Breastfed and Formula-Fed United States Infants and are Associated with Growth Status.
justification: 115 healthy full-term infants (4-5mo), exclusively BF (n=54) vs exclusively FF (n=61); 16S rRNA sequencing shows feeding type was the most significant variable on gut microbiota composition (P<1e-6) with alpha/beta diversity and taxon-level differences (Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Ruminococcaceae).

title: A health-promoting role of exclusive breastfeeding on infants through restoring delivery mode-induced gut microbiota perturbations.
justification: The feeding-pattern comparison in this cohort is exclusive breastfeeding (EBF, n=33) versus mixed feeding (MF, n=68, a combination of breast milk and formula); no exclusively formula-fed group exists, so no direct breastfed-vs-formula-fed contrast is reported.

title: Effect of Probiotic-Fortified Infant Formula on Infant Gut Health and Microbiota Modulation.
justification: RCT in 118 Korean infants with 3 groups: breast milk (BF, n=50), probiotic formula (PF, n=35), and unsupplemented placebo formula (FF, n=33); 16S NGS sequencing shows distinct fecal microbiota composition and alpha diversity between BF and FF groups.

title: Innova 2020: A Follow-Up Study of the Fecal Microbiota of Infants Using a Novel Infant Formula between 6 Months and 12 Months of Age.
justification: RCT in term infants (per AAP infant-formula testing criteria), 210 infants (70/group): novel INN formula (postbiotic+higher DHA/ARA), standard STD formula (unsupplemented comparator), and exclusively BF group; 16S V3-V4 sequencing shows significant phylum-level and alpha-diversity differences between STD and BF groups at 6 and 12 months.

title: Early development of infant gut microbiota in relation to breastfeeding and human milk oligosaccharides.
justification: All analyzed infants in the CBGS-BF cohort are exclusively breastfed, stratified only by EBF duration (under 3, 3 to 6, over 6 months); there is no formula-fed comparator group analyzed in this study's own data (formula-fed comparisons mentioned are citations of other studies).

title: The Relationship Between Diet, Gut Microbiota, and Serum Metabolome of South Asian Infants at 1 Year.
justification: START cohort, 182 healthy 1-year-old South Asian infants, 16S rRNA gene profiling; breastfed infants showed significantly higher abundance of Bifidobacterium (3.29 log2-fold) and Lactobacillus (7.93 log2-fold) compared to non-breastfed infants, a direct taxonomic composition comparison by feeding status.

title: Distinguishable Influence of the Delivery Mode, Feeding Pattern, and Infant Sex on Dynamic Alterations in the Intestinal Microbiota in the First Year of Life.
justification: The feeding-pattern comparison is exclusive breastfeeding (n=36) versus combined feeding (n=19, a mixture of breast milk and formula); no exclusively formula-fed group exists in this cohort, so no direct breastfed-vs-formula-fed contrast is reported.

title: Early life gut microbiota profiles linked to synbiotic formula effects: a randomized clinical trial in European infants.
justification: RCT, 540 healthy infants with 3 isolable groups: unsupplemented control formula (CF, n=230), synbiotic intervention formula (IF, n=230), and a directly-sampled human milk (HM) reference group (n=80); 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant diversity and taxonomic composition differences between CF and HM groups at month 4.

title: Effects of a Novel Infant Formula on the Fecal Microbiota in the First Six Months of Life: The INNOVA 2020 Study.
justification: Same INNOVA 2020 RCT as covidence #771 (companion 0-6 month report); 210 term infants (70/group): novel INN formula (postbiotic+higher DHA/ARA), standard STD formula (unsupplemented comparator), and exclusively BF group; 16S sequencing shows STD vs BF differ in richness, diversity, and genus-level composition (Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Clostridium, Lactobacillus) at 21 days, 2, and 6 months.

title: Environmental and genetic associations with aberrant early-life gut microbial maturation in childhood asthma.
justification: VDAART cohort, fecal 16S rRNA sequencing at 3-6 months and 1 year; direct differential abundance of specific taxa by breastfeeding status reported (Bifidobacterium beta=0.06, P=.03; Bacteroides beta=0.05, P=.01, both positively associated with exclusive breastfeeding at 3-6 months).

title: Human milk oligosaccharides, antimicrobial drugs, and the gut microbiota of term neonates: observations from the KOALA birth cohort study.
justification: KOALA birth cohort, 1023 term neonates, 16S rRNA sequencing at 1 month; proportion of breastfeeding explained the largest variation in microbiota composition (PERMANOVA), with breastfed infants showing significantly higher Bifidobacterium/Bacilli and lower Bacteroides/Veillonella/Clostridia relative abundance compared to formula-fed infants.

title: Breastfeeding enrichment of B. longum subsp. infantis mitigates the effect of antibiotics on the microbiota and childhood asthma risk.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study inclusion criterion is delivery after 35 weeks gestation, which includes late-preterm (35-36wk) infants, and no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis is reported (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155, #488, #614).

title: The gut microbiome of obese postpartum women with and without previous gestational diabetes mellitus and the gut microbiota of their babies.
justification: 84 mother-infant pairs, infants 2-6 months, 16S V4 sequencing; offspring exposed to exclusive breastfeeding showed significantly greater abundance of Bacteroides and Staphylococcus versus non-exclusively-breastfed infants, a direct taxonomic differential-abundance comparison by feeding status.

title: Mobile genetic elements from the maternal microbiome shape infant gut microbial assembly and metabolism.
justification: 74 infants born GA 36-42wk (term), shotgun metagenomic sequencing; PERMANOVA on species-level taxonomic composition (Bray-Curtis) shows significant effects of breastfeeding and formula use/type (regular, hydrolyzed, no formula), with regular formula linked to enrichment of E. faecalis, A. radingae, and S. thermophilus versus breastfed infants.

title: The Effect of Breast Milk Microbiota on the Composition of Infant Gut Microbiota: A Cohort Study.
justification: 23 healthy term infants (GA ~39wk) divided into breastfeeding group (BF, breastfed >=25 of first 30 days, n=13) and formula-predominant group (MF, formula-fed >=25 of first 30 days, n=10); 16S rRNA sequencing of infant stool shows distinct gut microbiota-SCFA correlation patterns and taxon-level differences between groups.

title: Effects of addition of 2-fucosyllactose to infant formula on growth and specific pathways of utilization by Bifidobacterium in healthy term infants.
justification: RCT, 221 healthy term infants with 3 arms: control formula (standard commercial formula, GOS/FOS/DHA/ARA at baseline), test formula (same plus added 2'FL), and breastfed reference; shotgun metagenomic sequencing shows both formula groups had significantly greater MGS richness and diversity than the breastfed group after 16 weeks, a direct composition comparison.

title: Gut microbe metabolism of small molecules supports human development across the early stages of life.
justification: Secondary analysis of 250 breastfed and 217 formula-fed healthy term infants (0-6mo) from public shotgun metagenomic datasets; PERMANOVA shows distinct taxonomic composition by feeding type, with significantly higher B. breve/B. bifidum and lower E. coli in breastfed vs formula-fed infants.

title: Breastfeeding might partially contribute to gut microbiota construction and stabilization of propionate metabolism in cesarean-section infants.
justification: The study explicitly states none of the 61 recruited infants was categorized as formula feeding type; the feeding comparison is exclusive breastfeeding versus mixed feeding (breast milk plus any other food/formula), with no exclusively formula-fed group.

title: Infant Formula With a Specific Blend of Five Human Milk Oligosaccharides Drives the Gut Microbiota Development and Improves Gut Maturation Markers: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants, 3 arms: control group (CG, standard IF without HMOs), TG1/TG2 (same IF with 1.5/2.5 g/L 5-HMO blend), and human milk group (HMG) reference; shotgun metagenomics at baseline, 3, and 6 months enables direct CG-vs-HMG composition comparison.

title: A synbiotics, long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, and milk fat globule membranes supplemented formula modulates microbiota maturation and neurodevelopment.
justification: COGNIS study, 170 full-term healthy infants with 3 isolable groups: unsupplemented standard formula (SF), SF supplemented with synbiotics/LC-PUFA/MFGM (EF), and breastfed reference (BF); 16S rRNA sequencing shows SF vs BF differ in enterotype trajectories, diversity, and genus-level abundance (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium) through 18 months.

title: Microbial Interrelationships across Sites of Breastfeeding Mothers and Infants at 6 Weeks Postpartum.
justification: The study explicitly states the authors intended to recruit an exclusively formula-fed reference group but were unable to; the comparison is exclusively breastfeeding (EBF, n=20) versus mixed-feeding (MF, human milk + formula, n=13), and feeding mode had no significant effect on infant stool (gut) microbiota composition.

title: Comparison of the Gut Microbiota in Healthy Infants With Different Delivery Modes and Feeding Types: A Cohort Study.
justification: 62 healthy term infants (GA 37-42wk) exclusively breastfed or exclusively formula-fed (no probiotics/prebiotics) for >4 months; 16S V4 sequencing at 40 days, 3, and 6 months shows significant alpha diversity and genus-level (Bifidobacterium, Streptococcus, Enterococcus) differences by feeding type within delivery-mode strata.

title: Metabolic Phenotype and Microbiome of Infants Fed Formula Containing Lactobacillus paracasei subsp. paracasei F19.
justification: RCT, healthy full-term infants, 151 subjects: standard formula (SF, unsupplemented), F19-supplemented formula, and breastfed reference (BF); 16S V4 sequencing shows SF and F19 infants had similar composition that was significantly different from BF infants at 4 months.

title: Longitudinal body mass index trajectories at preschool age: children with rapid growth have differential composition of the gut microbiota in the first year of life.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study (same recruitment: 3621 recruited, 3455 eligible, matching covidence #155/#488/#614/#835), whose inclusion criterion is delivery after 35 weeks gestation including late-preterm infants, with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup reported; also the primary exposure/outcome is BMI trajectory group, not a direct breastfed-vs-formula-fed composition comparison.

title: Early-life fecal microbiome and metabolome dynamics in response to an intervention with infant formula containing specific prebiotics and postbiotics.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants, 3 arms: standard unsupplemented control formula, prebiotic/postbiotic experimental formula, and exclusively breastfed reference; 16S rRNA sequencing shows multiple bacterial groups significantly different between control and breastfed arms.

title: Impact of Early Feeding: Metagenomics Analysis of the Infant Gut Microbiome.
justification: 34 healthy term infants (5-100 days), exclusively BF (n=24) vs exclusively FF (n=10, no antibiotics/hypoallergenic formula); shotgun metagenomic sequencing (NGS) shows 39 genera significantly differentially represented between BF and FF cohorts, including higher Bifidobacterium in BF.

title: Changes in the gut microbiota of Nigerian infants within the first year of life.
justification: Feeding groups are exclusively breastfed (EBF) versus mixed-fed (MF, breast plus formula combined); no exclusively formula-fed group exists. The cohort also explicitly includes both full-term and preterm infants (mean GA 37.6+-2.8wk) with no separable term-only subgroup.

title: Feeding Practice and Delivery Mode Are Determinants of Vitamin K in the Infant Gut: An Exploratory Analysis.
justification: STRONG Kids 2 cohort, 46 infants (23 breastfeeding, 23 formula-feeding) at 6 weeks; shotgun metagenomic sequencing shows relative abundances of 33 bacterial species significantly affected by feeding mode (P<0.05), a direct taxonomic composition comparison.

title: Exclusive breast-feeding, the early-life microbiome and immune response, and common childhood respiratory illnesses.
justification: INSPIRE study, 1949 healthy term infants (GA 38-40wk) with exclusive breast milk (n=667) vs exclusive formula (n=929) groups; 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant alpha/beta diversity differences and differential abundance of 3 gut genera (Escherichia-Shigella, Bifidobacterium, Clostridium innocuum) by type of feeding.

title: The establishment of the gut microbiota in 1-year-aged infants: from birth to family food.
justification: The non-exclusively-breastfed comparator group (NeBF) explicitly includes both exclusively formula-fed and mixed-fed infants combined, so no clean breastfed-vs-formula-fed contrast can be isolated.

title: Safety and efficacy of a probiotic-containing infant formula supplemented with 2'-fucosyllactose: a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
justification: Both formula arms contain the probiotic L. reuteri DSM 17938 (control group) with the experimental group additionally supplemented with 2'FL; no unsupplemented standard-formula arm exists to isolate against the breastfed reference group.

title: Effect of an infant formula containing sn-2 palmitate on fecal microbiota and metabolome profiles of healthy term infants: a randomized, double-blind, parallel, controlled study.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants, 3 groups: investigational (sn-2 palmitate formula), control (regular vegetable oil formula, unsupplemented), and breastfed; 16S rRNA sequencing at 8 and 16 weeks enables direct control-vs-breastfed composition comparison.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation in Exclusively Breastfed Infants Is Associated with Alterations in the Fecal Microbiome.
justification: 191 infants (3-9 months) classified as exclusively breastfed (n=88), partially breastfed (n=43), or not breastfed/exclusively formula-fed (n=60); 16S V4 sequencing shows significantly lower Shannon diversity and distinct PERMANOVA-significant composition (R2=4.1%, P<0.01) in exclusively breastfed vs not-breastfed infants.

title: Fecal Bacterial Communities Differ by Lactation Status in Postpartum Women and Their Infants.
justification: The comparison is exclusive human milk feeding (n=14) versus non-exclusive feeding (some formula feeding, n=10); the paper explicitly states all infants were still receiving at least some human milk, so no exclusively formula-fed group exists.

title: Mother's Milk Microbiome Shaping Fecal and Skin Microbiota in Infants with Food Allergy and Atopic Dermatitis: A Pilot Analysis.
justification: Pilot study including both allergic and healthy control infants; a separable healthy-only subgroup analysis compares breastfed vs formula-fed fecal/skin microbiota composition via 16S sequencing (PERMANOVA-significant structure differences, signature OTUs reported separately for the healthy group in Figures 5C and 6C).

title: Term infant formula supplemented with milk-derived oligosaccharides shifts the gut microbiota closer to that of human milk-fed infants and improves intestinal immune defense: a randomized controlled trial.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants, 3 groups: unsupplemented control formula (CG, n=112), MOS-supplemented experimental formula (EG, n=114), and human milk-fed reference (HFI, n=70); 16S-based microbiota analysis shows CG significantly differed from HFI in overall composition and bifidobacteria abundance at 2.5 and 4 months.

title: Impact of Maternal Intrapartum Antibiotics, and Caesarean Section with and without Labour on Bifidobacterium and Other Infant Gut Microbiota.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study inclusion criterion is singleton live birth at 35 weeks of gestation or later, which includes late-preterm (35-36wk) infants, with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis reported (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155, #488, #614, #835, #972).

title: The infant gut microbiota at 12 months of age is associated with human milk exposure but not with maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index or infant BMI-for-age z-scores.
justification: ARCHGUT/BABYGUT Michigan cohorts, 33 infants at 12 months; 16S V4 sequencing shows infants with no human milk exposure (exclusively formula-fed) had significantly distinct beta diversity (Sorensen distance) and alpha diversity (Chao1) compared to infants exposed to human milk.

title: Infant Feeding Alters the Longitudinal Impact of Birth Mode on the Developing Gut Microbiome.
justification: The study explicitly defines formula-fed (FF) as infants who were either exclusively formula-fed OR breastfed with formula supplementation (i.e., did not meet EBF criteria), conflating exclusively-formula and mixed-feeding into one comparator group, so no clean breastfed-vs-formula-fed contrast can be isolated.

title: Effects of Infant Formula Supplemented With Prebiotics and OPO on Infancy Fecal Microbiota: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
justification: RCT, full-term infants (GA 37-42wk), 108 infants: breastfeeding (n=59), standard formula (unsupplemented, n=18), and OPO/prebiotic-supplemented formula (n=31); 16S V4 sequencing at 4 months compares composition of standard formula vs breastfeeding groups directly.

title: Early Life Microbiota Colonization at Six Months of Age: A Transitional Time Point.
justification: The A.MA.MI. cohort NeBF (non-exclusively-breastfed) comparator group explicitly includes both exclusively formula-fed and mixed-fed infants combined (authors state this as a limitation preventing isolation of breastfeeding's specific effect), so no clean breastfed-vs-formula-fed contrast is reported.

title: Transient Effect of Infant Formula Supplementation on the Intestinal Microbiota.
justification: The comparison is exclusively breastfed infants versus infants supplemented with formula in addition to breastfeeding (mixed feeding); no exclusively formula-fed group exists in this cohort.

title: Key bacterial taxa and metabolic pathways affecting gut short-chain fatty acid profiles in early life.
justification: This is a longitudinal study of 12 infants analyzing within-subject temporal changes in SCFA-microbiota relationships across breastfeeding cessation and antibiotic exposure; there is no between-group breastfed-vs-formula-fed composition comparison reported.

title: Impact of synbiotics on gut microbiota during early life: a randomized, double-blind study.
justification: Microbiota composition was assessed using fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) and targeted qPCR for 7 pre-selected bacterial taxonomic groups, not sequencing-based taxonomic profiling.

title: Metagenomic analysis of the gut microbiome composition associated with vitamin D supplementation in Taiwanese infants.
justification: The 'formula-fed infants (FFI)' comparator group is explicitly defined as mixed-fed or formula-fed infants combined, conflating mixed feeding and exclusive formula feeding into one category, so no clean breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast can be isolated.

title: Environmental Tobacco Smoke Exposure and Breastfeeding Duration Influence the Composition and Dynamics of Gut Microbiota in Young Children Aged 0-2 Years.
justification: The primary design examines tobacco smoke exposure; breastfeeding is analyzed only as a continuous duration variable in multiple regression (correlated with Lactobacillus and Clostridium_sensu_stricto_1), with no defined formula-fed comparator group or reported between-group breastfed-vs-formula-fed composition statistics.

title: Breastfeeding restored the gut microbiota in caesarean section infants and lowered the infection risk in early life.
justification: 41 full-term infants (>37wk GA), fed pure human milk (B) or pure formula without prebiotics (F); 16S V3-V4 sequencing shows feeding pattern was the most dominant factor shaping gut microbiota in the first 6 months (PERMANOVA P=0.004), with Bifidobacterium less abundant in CS-formula infants, partially restored by breastfeeding.

title: Impact Of Feeding Practice On Diversity Pattern Of The Gut Microbiome In Infants.
justification: 46 healthy Pakistani infants (23 breastfed, 23 formula-fed), 0-4 months, excluding antibiotics/GI surgery; next-generation sequencing shows significant phylum/genus-level differences (Firmicutes, Bacilli, Streptococcaceae higher in FF; Selenomonadales, S. salivarius higher in BF).

title: Stool microbiome, pH and short/branched chain fatty acids in infants receiving extensively hydrolyzed formula, amino acid formula, or human milk through two months of age.
justification: Healthy term infants (37-42wk GA, no CMA or clinical indication), randomized to amino-acid formula (AAF, n=25) or extensively hydrolyzed formula (EHF, n=28), vs human milk reference (n=25); 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant alpha/beta diversity and taxon-level differences (Bifidobacterium higher in HM, Firmicutes higher in both formula groups) at Day 60.

title: Comparison of gut microbiota in exclusively breast-fed and formula-fed babies: a study of 91 term infants.
justification: 91 healthy term infants (GA 37-42wk), exclusively fed breast milk (n=30), formula A (n=30), or formula B (n=31) for >4 months; 16S V4 sequencing shows significant genus-level differences (Bifidobacterium, Bacteroides, Streptococcus, Enterococcus, Lachnospiraceae, Veillonella, Clostridioides) between breastfed and formula-fed groups at 40 days and 3 months.

title: From Birth to Overweight and Atopic Disease: Multiple and Common Pathways of the Infant Gut Microbiome.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study (1667 infants), which recruits infants delivered after 35 weeks gestation including late-preterm infants with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155/#488/#614/#835/#972/#1069); additionally, the primary exposure is birth mode/prolonged labor mediated through the microbiome via structural equation modeling, not a direct breastfed-vs-formula-fed composition comparison.

title: Human Milk Feeding Patterns at 6 Months of Age are a Major Determinant of Fecal Bacterial Diversity in Infants.
justification: ARCHGUT/BABYGUT Michigan cohorts, 36 infants at 6 months grouped into 4 human-milk-exposure categories (100%, 80%, 50-80%, <=20%, the latter predominantly formula); 16S V4 sequencing with PERMANOVA shows significant beta diversity differences across these feeding categories (Figure 1D-F, Table 5), with human milk exposure explaining 20% of alpha diversity variation.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals the influence of genetic and environmental risk factors on developing gut microbiota in infants at risk of celiac disease.
justification: 31 healthy infants (genetically at risk for celiac disease via first-degree relative, but not themselves diagnosed with any disease) from the CDGEMM cohort; shotgun metagenomic sequencing shows significant species-level differences between exclusive formula feeding and exclusive breastmilk feeding (e.g., B. adolescentis, S. epidermidis, R. gnavus; Fig 2, P<0.05) at enrollment, 3, and 4-6 months.

title: Fermented infant formula (with Bifidobacterium breve C50 and Streptococcus thermophilus O65) with prebiotic oligosaccharides is safe and modulates the gut microbiota towards a microbiota closer to that of breastfed infants.
justification: Fecal microbiota composition was determined using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) with a panel of targeted 16S-rRNA probes for pre-selected bacterial groups, not sequencing-based taxonomic profiling.

title: Lactose-reduced infant formula with added corn syrup solids is associated with a distinct gut microbiota in Hispanic infants.
justification: 91 Hispanic infants at 6 months, 4 groups: human milk from breast (BB), pumped human milk (BP), traditional unsupplemented formula (TF), and lactose-reduced formula with added sugar (ASF); 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant MDS separation and family-level differences (Bifidobacteriaceae, Lachnospiraceae) between TF/ASF and BB/BP groups.

title: Breastmilk Feeding Practices Are Associated with the Co-Occurrence of Bacteria in Mothers' Milk and the Infant Gut: the CHILD Cohort Study.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study inclusion criterion is delivery after 35 weeks gestation, which includes late-preterm (35-36wk) infants, and no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis is reported (same cohort/inclusion issue as covidence #155, #488, #614, #835, #972, #1069, #1234).

title: Analysis of immune, microbiota and metabolome maturation in infants in a clinical trial of Lactobacillus paracasei CBA L74-fermented formula.
justification: RCT, healthy full-term infants, 3 groups (n=13/group, stratified by delivery mode): standard unsupplemented formula, L. paracasei-fermented formula, and breastfeeding reference; 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant diversity differences for vaginally-delivered standard-formula vs breastfed infants at visit 2.

title: Ethnic diversity in infant gut microbiota is apparent before the introduction of complementary diets.
justification: GUSTO Singapore birth cohort, 106 infants at 3 months grouped as breastfed only (n=16), mixed (n=33), or formula only (n=56); 16S V4 sequencing with partial CCA shows significant OTU-level differences by feeding status (Bacteroides higher in breastfed-only; Staphylococcus, Erysipelatoclostridium, Intestinibacter higher in formula-only).

title: Early Effect of Supplemented Infant Formulae on Intestinal Biomarkers and Microbiota: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
justification: RCT, 203 healthy term infants, groups: unsupplemented control formula (F, n=40), two supplemented formulas (FLP, FLPP), and breastfed reference (BF, n=61); 16S rRNA sequencing with CCA shows F and FLP groups significantly separated from the BF group at 1, 4, and 8 weeks.

title: Distinct Gut Microbiota and Metabolite Profiles Induced by Different Feeding Methods in Healthy Chinese Infants.
justification: 77 healthy Chinese infants (median GA 38 weeks), excluding antibiotic/probiotic exposure, in 4 feeding groups: exclusively breastfed (BF), mixed-fed (MF), exclusively formula-fed (FF), complementary food-fed (CF); 16S V3-V4 sequencing shows distinct genus-level enrichment by group (Bifidobacterium/Lactobacillus in BF; Bacteroides/Blautia in FF) with direct BF-vs-FF statistical comparison (Figure 1B).

title: A systematic machine learning and data type comparison yields metagenomic predictors of infant age, sex, breastfeeding, antibiotic usage, country of origin, and delivery type.
justification: This is a machine-learning methods paper using the DIABIMMUNE cohort (samples spanning up to 36 months) to build classifiers predicting breastfeeding status as one of several phenotypic targets; it reports model prediction accuracy and feature importance, not a direct epidemiological comparison of taxonomic composition (alpha/beta diversity or differential abundance) between breastfed and formula-fed groups.

title: Neonatal diet alters fecal microbiota and metabolome profiles at different ages in infants fed breast milk or formula.
justification: Healthy term infants (GA ~39wk) from the Beginnings Study, exclusively BF, dairy-based formula (MF), or soy-based formula (SF) groups at 3,6,9,12 months; 16S sequencing shows BF had lowest alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium was 2.6-5-fold lower in SF vs BF through 1 year.

title: Prenatal and postnatal determinants in shaping offspring's microbiome in the first 1000 days: study protocol and preliminary results at one month of life.
justification: A.MA.MI cohort, 60 healthy term infants (GA 37-42wk), at 1 month (T1) classified cleanly as breastfed (n=34) vs formula-fed (n=24), unlike this cohort's later-timepoint papers which conflate mixed feeding into the comparator; 16S rRNA sequencing shows significant genus and species-level composition differences between BF and FF infants (Fig 3d).

title: Microbiome Study of Initial Gut Microbiota from Newborn Infants to Children Reveals that Diet Determines Its Compositional Development.
justification: Korean newborns (natural delivery), 2 breast-milk-fed (BM1) vs 7 formula-milk-fed (FM1) infants in the first week of life; 16S rRNA sequencing shows Bifidobacterium increased to 35.1% in BM1 by third sample, while Klebsiella and Serratia emerged in FM1 (4.4% and 34.2%), a direct composition comparison.

title: Linking Human Milk Oligosaccharides, Infant Fecal Community Types, and Later Risk To Require Antibiotics.
justification: RCT, healthy term infants, 3 groups: unsupplemented control formula (n=63), HMO-supplemented test formula (n=58), and breastfed reference (BF, n=35); 16S rRNA sequencing at 3 and 12 months shows control-group microbiota alpha/beta diversity and fecal community type distribution significantly differ from BF.

title: Neonatal microbiota development and the effect of early life antibiotics are determined by two distinct settler types.
justification: Microbial composition was analyzed using IS-pro, a PCR-based fragment-length fingerprinting technique (16S-23S rRNA interspace region length polymorphism with phylum-specific primers), not next-generation DNA sequencing; this is a fingerprinting method analogous to DGGE/TGGE rather than sequencing-based taxonomic profiling.

title: Development of the Microbiota and Associations With Birth Mode, Diet, and Atopic Disorders in a Longitudinal Analysis of Stool Samples, Collected From Infancy Through Early Childhood.
justification: All but 6 of 440 children were breastfed for varying durations; the diet exposure analyzed is cessation of breastfeeding over time (within-subject longitudinal change), not a between-group breastfed-vs-formula-fed comparison, and there is no exclusively formula-fed comparator group.

title: Clostridioides difficile Colonization Is Differentially Associated With Gut Microbiome Profile, Metabolome and Secretory Immunoglobulin A in Exclusively Breastfed, Partially Breastfed, and Formula-fed Infants.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study (same recruitment/eligibility criteria as covidence #155/#488/#614/#835/#972/#1069/#1234/#1273), which includes infants delivered after 35 weeks gestation with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis reported.

title: Alterations in the Gut Microbiome at 6 Months of Age in Obese Latino Infants.
justification: The comparison is exclusively breastfed infants (n=22 at 4-6 weeks, n=4 at 6 months) versus all other infants combined (mixed-fed and formula-fed together); no isolated exclusively-formula-fed comparator group is reported.

title: Fecal microbiome and metabolome of infants fed bovine MFGM supplemented formula or standard formula with breast-fed infants as reference: a randomized controlled trial.
justification: RCT, 90 infants (GA 37-42wk), 3 groups: unsupplemented standard formula (SF), bovine MFGM-supplemented experimental formula (EF), and exclusively breastfed (BF) reference; 16S V4 sequencing at 2, 4, 6, 12 months enables direct SF-vs-BF microbiome composition comparison.

title: Compositional analyses reveal correlations between taxon-level gut bacterial abundance and peripheral T cell marker expression in African infants.
justification: The comparison is exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) versus nonexclusive breastfeeding (NEBF), explicitly defined as breastmilk combined with other liquids/solids or formula; this conflates mixed feeding and formula feeding into one comparator group, so no clean breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast can be isolated.

title: Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus Composition at Species Level and Gut Microbiota Diversity in Infants before 6 Weeks.
justification: 112 term Han infants (GA 39.7wk), groups defined as BF (breast milk sole source, n=41), MPF (mixed breast milk+formula, n=39), and MF (infant formula sole source, n=32); 16S V3-V4 plus groEL gene sequencing shows significant genus/species-level differences in Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus composition between BF and MF (exclusively formula) groups.

title: Dynamic signatures of gut microbiota and influences of delivery and feeding modes during the first 6 months of life.
justification: 102 healthy term Chinese infants (GA 39wk), classified into breastfeeding-dominant (BFD) vs formula-feeding-dominant (FFD) groups (>=50% duration criterion); 16S V3-V4 sequencing with PCoA and LEfSe shows significant genus-level differences (Haemophilus higher in BFD; Enterococcus, Lactococcus, Peptoclostridium higher in FFD) at 42 days, 3, and 6 months.

title: Early limited formula for breastfeeding infants: too much or just enough?
justification: This is an evidence-based commentary on a separate primary RCT (Flaherman et al. 2018, J Pediatr); it presents no new primary data of its own.

title: Whole genome metagenomic analysis of the gut microbiome of differently fed infants identifies differences in microbial composition and functional genes, including an absent CRISPR/Cas9 gene in the formula-fed cohort.
exclusion_reason: Duplicate report of an already-included cohort
justification: Same research group, institution (Nemours), lead author, study design (shotgun metagenomics, breast-fed vs formula-fed infants ~45-100 days old) as covidence #989 (Di Guglielmo et al., 2022, 10.3389/fcimb.2022.816601); this 2019 paper's n=10 BF/n=5 FF appears to be an earlier, smaller pilot subset of the later expanded cohort (n=24 BF/n=10 FF) already included under #989.

title: The Perturbation of Infant Gut Microbiota Caused by Cesarean Delivery Is Partially Restored by Exclusive Breastfeeding.
justification: The feeding-pattern comparison is exclusive breastfeeding (n=67) versus mixed feeding (breast milk and formula, n=27); no exclusively formula-fed group exists in this cohort.

title: Michigan cohorts to determine associations of maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index with pregnancy and infant gastrointestinal microbial communities: Late pregnancy and early infancy.
justification: ARCHGUT/BABYGUT cohorts; the reported breastfeeding comparisons are explicitly exclusively breastfed versus mixed-diet infants (e.g., 'the same associations were observed when comparing exclusively breastfed and mixed diet infants'), not breastfed versus exclusively formula-fed.

title: The effect of prebiotic fortified infant formulas on microbiota composition and dynamics in early life.
justification: Healthy term infants (>37wk GA) from two Dutch cohorts: KOALA (2002-03, traditional unsupplemented formula vs breastfed) and BINGO (2015-16, GOS/FOS-fortified formula vs breastfed); 16S rRNA sequencing shows KOALA FF infants had reduced Bifidobacterium/Lactobacillus and higher Clostridium/Escherichia-Shigella vs BF, a direct within-cohort unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed comparison.

title: Breastfeeding: a key modulator of gut microbiota characteristics in late infancy.
justification: The comparison is children still breastfed versus children no longer breastfed, where the latter group explicitly combines those who were 'formula-fed or mixed-fed'; no isolated breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast is reported.

title: Infant diet and maternal gestational weight gain predict early metabolic maturation of gut microbiomes.
justification: Twin birth cohort with median gestational age 37 weeks (IQR 36-38), indicating a substantial proportion of infants born preterm/late-preterm, with no separable >=37wk-only subgroup analysis reported.

title: Probiotic supplementation restores normal microbiota composition and function in antibiotic-treated and in caesarean-born infants.
justification: RCT in infants with family history of allergy (not a current clinical condition), 428 infants at 3 months; placebo arm (sugar syrup only, no GOS/probiotic) comprised 201 breastfed and 22 formula-fed infants, with diet reported as a significant modifier of microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing plus metagenomics); only breastfed infants in the probiotic arm showed the expected Bifidobacterium increase, with B. breve dominance differing starkly by feeding type within the control group (12% breastfed vs 0% formula-fed).

title: Maternal gut and breast milk microbiota affect infant gut antibiotic resistome and mobile genetic elements.
justification: This study examines breastfeeding duration (shorter vs. longer than 6 months) and maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis in relation to the infant gut antibiotic resistome and mobile genetic elements; there is no formula-fed comparator group, and the outcomes reported are resistome/MGE composition rather than bacterial taxonomic composition.

title: Diet during Pregnancy and Infancy and the Infant Intestinal Microbiome.
justification: VDAART cohort, 323 infants, 16S rRNA sequencing (454 pyrosequencing) of stool at 3-6 months; breastfeeding vs formula feeding was independently and most consistently associated with infant microbial diversity and specific taxa (e.g., Bifidobacterium), a direct composition comparison.

title: Intestinal Inflammation in Chilean Infants Fed With Bovine Formula vs. Breast Milk and Its Association With Their Gut Microbiota.
justification: 25 healthy term infants (38-42wk GA), 15 breast milk (BM) vs 10 bovine formula-predominant (BF, >=20% formula) groups; 16S rRNA 454 pyrosequencing shows significant phylum-level (Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio) and genus-level (Enterococcus, Streptococcus, Enterobacter) composition differences between BM and BF groups at 1 month, with RDA confirming significant community structure difference.

title: Association of Exposure to Formula in the Hospital and Subsequent Infant Feeding Practices With Gut Microbiota and Risk of Overweight in the First Year of Life.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study (1087 infants, same recruitment/eligibility as covidence #155/#488/#614/#835/#972/#1069/#1234/#1273/#1365), which includes infants delivered after 35 weeks gestation with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis reported.

title: Feeding-Related Gut Microbial Composition Associates With Peripheral T-Cell Activation and Mucosal Gene Expression in African Infants.
justification: The comparison is exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) versus nonexclusive breastfeeding (NEBF), defined as any non-breast milk feeds (which could include mixed feeding or formula combined); this is the parent study of covidence #1423 and shares the same conflated comparator, with no isolated breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast.

title: HIV-exposure, early life feeding practices and delivery mode impacts on faecal bacterial profiles in a South African birth cohort.
justification: Drakenstein Child Health Study, South Africa, median GA 39wk, HIV-exposed-uninfected (not diseased) and HIV-unexposed infants combined; 16S V4 sequencing shows exclusively breastfed vs exclusively formula-fed infants at discharge had significantly different composition (Proteobacteria/Actinobacteria higher in BF; Enterobacteriaceae/Enterococcus/Streptococcus higher in FF), and a clean 3-group (exclusive BF/mixed/exclusive FF) diversity comparison at 4-12 weeks.

title: The Effect of Early Limited Formula on Breastfeeding, Readmission, and Intestinal Microbiota: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
justification: RCT design is exclusive breastfeeding (control) versus breastfeeding supplemented with 10mL early limited formula after each feed (intervention, a mixed-feeding protocol); there is no exclusively formula-fed arm.

title: Galacto-Oligosaccharide/Polidextrose Enriched Formula Protects against Respiratory Infections in Infants at High Risk of Atopy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
justification: Microbiota composition was quantified using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) with species-specific probes, not sequencing-based taxonomic profiling.

title: Perturbations of gut microbiome genes in infants with atopic dermatitis according to feeding type.
justification: 129 6-month-old Korean infants, including a separable healthy (non-AD) subgroup (n=66) analyzed by feeding type (breast milk, formula, mixed) via 16S pyrosequencing and whole-metagenome sequencing (subset); within the healthy group, observed OTU richness differed significantly by feeding type (lowest in breastfed, highest in mixed-fed, P<.01), with formula-fed richness also reported separately.

title: Does the maternal vaginal microbiota play a role in seeding the microbiota of neonatal gut and nose?
justification: The study explicitly states the dataset contained only 2 exclusively formula-fed infants, precluding any comparison to a formula-fed-only group; the feeding comparisons reported are vaginally-delivered-mixed-fed vs vaginally-delivered-breastfed vs caesarean-mixed-fed, not breastfed vs exclusively formula-fed.

title: Cesarean Section, Formula Feeding, and Infant Antibiotic Exposure: Separate and Combined Impacts on Gut Microbial Changes in Later Infancy.
justification: CHILD Cohort Study (same recruitment/eligibility as covidence #155/#488/#614/#835/#972/#1069/#1234/#1273/#1365/#1573), which includes infants delivered after 35 weeks gestation with no separate >=37wk-only subgroup analysis reported.

title: Intestinal microbiota in infants at high risk for allergy: Effects of prebiotics and role in eczema development.
justification: PATCH trial, infants with parental allergy history (not a current clinical condition), vaginally-born subset with breastfed (n=30), pHF-OS formula (n=51), and unsupplemented standard cow's milk formula control (n=57); 16S rRNA sequencing shows pHF-OS and standard formula groups differ significantly in Bifidobacterium, Clostridium, and Lachnospiraceae abundance, with standard formula group diverging more from the breastfed reference.

title: Intestinal colonisation patterns in breastfed and formula-fed infants during the first 12 weeks of life reveal sequential microbiota signatures.
justification: Longitudinal study of 4 exclusively breastfed and 4 exclusively formula-fed healthy term infants (>39wk gestation), all vaginally delivered, with a clean feeding-mode comparison; microbiota profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing plus qPCR confirmation, reporting higher Bifidobacterium dentium-like taxon, Enterococcus, and C. difficile in formula-fed vs breastfed infants.

title: Association Between Breast Milk Bacterial Communities and Establishment and Development of the Infant Gut Microbiome.
justification: 107 healthy full-term mother-infant pairs (antibiotic-exposed excluded), stool profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing; random forest analysis comparing exclusively vs nonexclusively breastfed infants found Ruminococcaceae and Bacteroidaceae more abundant in formula feeders, a direct taxonomic BF-vs-FF contrast alongside the dose-dependent breast-milk-intake analysis.

title: Ethnic and diet-related differences in the healthy infant microbiome.
justification: The exposure analyzed is ethnicity (CHILD white-Caucasian vs START South Asian cohorts) with 'breastfeeding status at time of collection' (still nursing vs not, at age ~1 year) used as a covariate; the 'not breastfeeding' group conflates formula, cow's-milk, and solids-only feeding (formula use itself tracked as a separate, non-defining covariate), so no clean exclusively-breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast is isolated or reported.

title: Starter formula enriched in prebiotics and probiotics ensures normal growth of infants and promotes gut health: a randomized clinical trial.
justification: Fecal bacterial analysis was performed by fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) and culture-based bacteriological counts (bifidobacteria, lactobacilli, clostridia/eubacteria) in Test, Control (unsupplemented formula), and breastfed-reference groups; no 16S or other sequencing-based taxonomic profiling was used.

title: Factors Influencing the Infant Gut Microbiome at Age 3-6 months: Findings from the ethnically diverse Vitamin D Antenatal Asthma Reduction Trial (VDAART).
justification: 333 infants (mean gestational age 39.1wk) from the VDAART cohort stratified into exclusively breastfed, breastfed-with-formula, and exclusively formula-fed (reference) groups, profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing; multivariate analysis found reduced Clostridiales (Clostridium, Ruminococcus, Coprococcus, Eubacterium) specifically in exclusively breastfed vs exclusively formula-fed infants.

title: Joint effects of pregnancy, sociocultural, and environmental factors on early life gut microbiome structure and diversity.
justification: 298 infants from the WHEALS Detroit birth cohort profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing, with breastfeeding practice at 1-month classified as exclusive, current-but-not-exclusive, or none (i.e., formula-fed); zero-inflated negative binomial models report specific taxa (e.g., increased Streptococcus, decreased Roseburia with exclusive breastfeeding in neonates; increased Lactobacillus, decreased Clostridia/Faecalibacterium/Ruminococcus with exclusive breastfeeding in infants) differentiating exclusively breastfed from non-breastfed infants.

title: Early Gut Microbiota Perturbations Following Intrapartum Antibiotic Prophylaxis to Prevent Group B Streptococcal Disease.
justification: Primary exposure is maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) for GBS; the only feeding groups studied are exclusively breastfed (BF) versus mixed-fed (MF) infants, with no exclusively formula-fed group recruited or compared.

title: Antibiotics, birth mode, and diet shape microbiome maturation during early life.
justification: Although infants were classified by dominant feeding mode (breast- vs formula-dominant) in the first 3 months, the paper's only reported statistically significant feeding-associated differences in diversity, maturation, and taxa (Fig. 2G-I, S8) occur specifically during the 12-24 month sampling window, outside the review's 0-12 month stool-sampling eligibility criterion.

title: Infant Gut Microbiota Development Is Driven by Transition to Family Foods Independent of Maternal Obesity.
justification: Breastfeeding is analyzed only as a continuous duration-of-exclusive-breastfeeding variable correlated with taxon abundance at 9 months (SKOT I/II cohorts); no infants were exclusively formula-fed and no exclusively-breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed group contrast is defined or reported, with formula appearing only as one minor component of the complementary-diet food-group PCA.

title: Effect of Infant Formula Containing a Low Dose of the Probiotic Bifidobacterium lactis CNCM I-3446 on Immune and Gut Functions in C-Section Delivered Babies: A Pilot Study.
justification: Both formula arms (n=77 each) contained the probiotic B. lactis at either low or regular dose, with a breastfed reference group; no unsupplemented-formula control group was included, so an unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast cannot be isolated.

title: Gut microbiota analysis reveals a marked shift to bifidobacteria by a starter infant formula containing a synbiotic of bovine milk-derived oligosaccharides and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis CNCM I-3446.
justification: 115 healthy full-term infants randomized to unsupplemented control formula (C, n=37), synbiotic test formula (T, n=39), or exclusively breastfed reference (B, n=39); 16S rRNA gene pyrosequencing shows the unsupplemented control formula group, but not the test group, differed from the breastfed reference in faecal pH and microbial diversity, giving an isolable unsupplemented-formula-vs-breastfed contrast.

title: Impact of maternal intrapartum antibiotics, method of birth and breastfeeding on gut microbiota during the first year of life: a prospective cohort study.
justification: 198 healthy full-term infants (CHILD Study Winnipeg subsample), stool profiled by Illumina 16S rRNA sequencing at 3 and 12 months; although the primary exposure is intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis, breastfeeding exclusivity (exclusively breastfed, partial, not breastfed/formula) is directly analyzed against taxa independent of IAP (Table S6), finding breastfeeding exclusivity inversely associated with Bacteroidetes and Clostridiales and positively with Proteobacteria/Actinobacteria at 3 months.

title: Comparison of the gut microbiota profile in breast-fed and formula-fed Korean infants using pyrosequencing.
justification: 20 healthy full-term, vaginally-delivered 4-week-old Korean infants (premature, antibiotic-exposed, and C-section infants excluded), 10 exclusively breastfed vs 10 formula-fed (70-100% formula) analyzed by pyrosequencing; found higher Actinobacteria/Bifidobacterium/B. longum in breastfed and higher Firmicutes/Proteobacteria/diversity in formula-fed infants.

title: Dynamics and Stabilization of the Human Gut Microbiome during the First Year of Life.
justification: 98 full-term Swedish mother-infant pairs profiled by metagenomic shotgun sequencing across the first year; at 4 months, exclusively breastfed vs exclusively formula-fed infants showed distinct MetaOTU profiles (higher Lactobacillus/B. longum in breastfed; higher C. difficile, Enterobacter, B. adolescentis in formula-fed) and differing functional (KO module) composition.

title: Milk- and solid-feeding practices and daycare attendance are associated with differences in bacterial diversity, predominant communities, and metabolic and immune function of the infant gut microbiome.
justification: The paper explicitly states 'no infants received formula exclusively'; the comparator group (non-EBF) is defined as infants receiving both breastmilk and formula (mixed feeding), not exclusively formula-fed, so no clean breastfed-vs-exclusively-formula-fed contrast is isolated.

title: Fecal Microbiota Composition of Breast-fed Infants is Correlated with Human Milk Oligosaccharides Consumed.
justification: Healthy, full-term, vaginally-delivered infants exclusively breastfed (n=16) or exclusively formula-fed (n=6) from birth, stool profiled at 3 months by 16S rRNA pyrosequencing; BF infants had higher Bacteroides and lower Clostridium XVIII, Streptococcus, Enterococcus, and Veillonella than FF infants (P<0.05). CONFIRMED COHORT OVERLAP: same University of Illinois recruitment protocol/IRB and formula brand (Enfamil LIPIL) as covidence #2022 (Schwartz et al. 2012) -- this paper explicitly cites #2022 for its DNA-extraction protocol and cites the same underlying Chapkin et al. 2010 cohort paper (not separately in this corpus) for recruitment/eligibility criteria. Identical FF group size (n=6) in both papers strongly suggests the same or near-identical formula-fed subjects; this paper's breastfed arm is larger (n=16 vs. #2022's n=6). Kept as Include alongside #2022 since the outcome here (HMO composition correlated with fecal microbiota taxa) is distinct from and non-redundant with #2022's transcriptome-microbiome virulence analysis. Review team should treat #1882 and #2022 as partially overlapping-sample evidence (not fully independent) at synthesis.

title: Impact of lifestyle on the gut microbiota of healthy infants and their mothers - the ALADDIN birth cohort.
justification: 128 healthy mother-infant pairs from the ALADDIN Swedish birth cohort, stool profiled by 454-pyrosequencing of 16S rRNA genes at 6 days, 3 weeks, 2 months, and 6 months; at 6 months, exclusively breastfed infants had the highest Bifidobacterium abundance, partly breastfed intermediate, and not-breastfed (formula) infants the lowest, with breastfed infants also showing lower Clostridiales abundance than non-breastfed infants.

title: Impact of Diet in Shaping Gut Microbiota Revealed by a Comparative Study in Infants During the First Six Months of Life.
exclusion_reason: Duplicate report of an already-included cohort
justification: Duplicate Covidence citation record of the same paper as covidence #5430 (Fan et al. 2014, DOI 10.4014/jmb.1309.09029 -- same manuscript, imported twice under slightly different title text: '...during the six months of life' here vs. '...during the first six months of life' at #5430). #5430 is retained as Include (already voted); #1948 is excluded as the duplicate record per criterion 10, rather than mirroring Include on both, to avoid this single paper being double-extracted into the synthesis.

title: Diversity of the intestinal microbiota in different patterns of feeding infants by Illumina high-throughput sequencing.
justification: 12 healthy infants (3-6 months, Hebei Province, China, all vaginally delivered, no significant difference in gestational age between groups) divided into exclusively breast-fed (n=6) and exclusively formula-fed (n=6); Illumina high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing found BF infants had significant enrichment of Actinobacteria/Firmicutes and depletion of Proteobacteria versus FF infants.

title: Human milk metagenome: a functional capacity analysis.
justification: This study's own primary data collection and analysis is the human milk metagenome (pooled sample from 10 donors); the breastfed- and formula-fed-infants' fecal metagenomes used for comparison are explicitly 'previously reported and publicly available' data reused from other studies via MG-RAST, not new infant stool samples collected or primarily analyzed in this paper.

title: Comparison of the compositions of the stool microbiotas of infants fed goat milk formula, cow milk-based formula, or breast milk.
justification: 90 healthy term Australian infants (gestational age 37-42 weeks) randomized to goat milk formula, cow milk-based formula, or a breastfed reference group (n=30 each), stool profiled by 16S rRNA pyrosequencing at 2 months; cow milk formula-fed infants showed more diverse Lachnospiraceae than breastfed infants, who were restricted mostly to Ruminococcus gnavus.

title: Gut microbiota of healthy Canadian infants: profiles by mode of delivery and infant diet at 4 months.
justification: 24 healthy term infants from the CHILD birth cohort, stool profiled at 4 months by high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing (V5-V7); exclusively breastfed (n=10) vs not-breastfed/formula-fed (n=9) infants compared directly, with formula-fed infants showing significantly higher Peptostreptococcaceae/C. difficile prevalence (71% vs 20%, P=0.01) and greater species richness.

title: Effect of breast and formula feeding on gut microbiota shaping in newborns.
justification: This is a narrative mini-review synthesizing prior literature on breast- vs formula-feeding and gut microbiota development, with no original subjects, methods, or data collected by the authors.

title: A metagenomic study of diet-dependent interaction between gut microbiota and host in infants reveals differences in immune response.
justification: Healthy full-term infants exclusively breast-fed (n=6) or formula-fed (n=6), stool collected at 3 months and profiled by metagenomic sequencing; microbiome OTU composition and functional (virulence-gene) content differed significantly between BF and FF infants, correlating with host immune-gene expression.
